def: A simple method evaluated the same way as the real model, setting the level any serious model must beat.
A predictor that ignores the features, such as always predicting the majority class or the training mean.
Predicting the most common class for every case, which sets the accuracy any classifier must exceed.
The number of positives found in a selected group divided by the number expected if the same number of cases were chosen at random.
The mean of the precision values at each rank where a true positive appears, summarising a ranking on rare positives.
Resampling the same test rows with replacement and recomputing two models' scores each time to get an interval for their difference.
The error that remains even for a perfect model because the target contains randomness no features explain.
A check on the pipeline rather than the problem, such as training on shuffled labels and expecting chance-level results.
Retraining with randomly permuted training labels; any held-out score above chance signals a leak or bug.
One minus the ratio of a model's squared error to that of always predicting the mean, so zero means no better than the mean baseline.
